instructions: Trim the green beans and cut them into 2-inch lengths. Peel the carrots and cut them into matchsticks. Chop the onion, mince 1 tbsp of the ginger and mince the 4 garlic cloves.
Heat the oil in a large skillet over medium heat. Add the onion and 1/4 tsp of the salt and cook for 8 minutes, stirring now and then, until it's soft and golden at the edges.
Add the ginger and garlic and stir for 1 minute, until it smells fragrant.
Add the tomato paste and cook for 1 minute, until it darkens. Add the diced tomatoes with their juice and the pepper and cook for 2 minutes.
Add the green beans, the carrots and 1 tbsp of water. Stir well, cover and cook for 12 minutes, stirring now and then, until the beans are almost tender. Add a splash of water if the pan looks dry.
Take the lid off and cook for 6 minutes, stirring, until the beans and carrots are tender and the sauce coats them.
Taste it. If it's flat, add the last 1/4 tsp of salt or a pinch more.
Serve warm or at room temperature.
method_notes: Neither version read shows a rating, so this follows Together Women Rise, which cooks onion, ginger and garlic down first, adds tomato paste and tomatoes, then steams the beans and carrots with a little water and finishes uncovered. Green Heart Garden skips the paste, uses turmeric, cumin and cardamom, and finishes with lemon; Eleni's Kitchen keeps it to onion, garlic and ginger with an optional potato. The lead's ratios are scaled to 4 servings, with no heat added.
